subject: general
question: The magnitudes of the magnetic field at a point at distance r from a straight conductor carrying current I, 2I and 3I, one by one, are B₁, B₂ and B₃, respectively. Which of the following relations is correct?
solution:
The correct answer is **B3 > B2 > B1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **magnitude** of a magnetic field at a point at **distance r** from a straight conductor carrying **current 'I'** is:
 
• B = (u₀)/(2pi) (I)/(r)
 
• **As the magnitude of the magnetic field directly depends upon the current carried by the straight conductor.**
 
• Thus,** the higher the current** carried by the conductor,** the higher will be the magnitude** of the magnetic field at a point at distance r.

Thus, In the given problem, **B3>B2>B1, as the current is 3I>2I>I.**
